**Method 1**

When we add a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always twice the real part of the complex number.

For the given complex number $z=3+5\text{i},$ the real part is $Re(z)=3,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =2\text{Re}(z) \\  & =2(3) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of adding the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=3+5\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=3-5\text{i}.$

Adding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =(3+5\text{i})+(3-5\text{i}) \\  & =(3+3)+\text{i}(5-5) \\  & =6+\text{i}0 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
